assetType: browser WebP conversion of NASA/GSFC PGDA LOLA derived hillshade; no annotations added
sourceDescription: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center Planetary Geology, Geophysics and Geochemistry Laboratory LOLA hillshade for 80°S to the south pole, generated from the LOLA 80S/80MPP adjusted DEM; stated hillshade illumination is 45° altitude and 45° azimuth.

projection.name: South polar stereographic
projection.coordinateFrame: MOON_ME reference frame of JPL DE421 ephemeris
projection.orientation: 0°E is up; 90°E is right; longitude positive east; image x=(xMeters+304000)/80 and image y=(304000-yMeters)/80.
projection.mappingFormula: rho = 2*1737400*tan((90-abs(latitude))/2); xMeters = rho*sin(longitude); yMeters = rho*cos(longitude); xPx=(xMeters+304000)/80; yPx=(304000-yMeters)/80; percentages use the full 7600×7600 canvas.
projection.sourceStatement: PGDA states that all TIF files are cloud-optimized GeoTIFFs with south polar stereographic X/Y coordinates in meters in the MOON_ME reference frame; the downloaded file's embedded GeoTIFF tags provide the scale and tiepoint used here.

featureNamingNote: Malapert pin is the IAU/USGS Malapert crater (Feature 3603), not Mons Malapert massif (Feature 16338).
webTransform: Uniform downsampling of the full square raster. Geographic percentages unchanged; no crop or annotation.
